Hi Sophie — thanks for flagging this and for the screenshot. Sorry for the friction.

Short answer: we expect the Calendly link to reflect the visitor's timezone, but sometimes links that don't force a TZ parameter end up creating the ICS without an explicit TZ, which can display as UTC in some calendar clients. Marcus, can you confirm the pattern here?

Quick technical note from infra side — we see this occasionally when the Calendly/Chili link is embedded without a tz parameter and the customer's browser picks display TZ but the generated ics uses Z/UTC because DTSTART/DTEND were emitted as floating times. Two practical workarounds we've used: 

- Manual ICS with TZID: create the event in Europe/Paris (or target TZ) so the ICS contains a TZID block, not Z. That's the most reliable.
- Use the scheduling link with an explicit parameter: ?timezone=Europe%2FParis or Chili Piper's force_timezone flag when building the URL.

For customers on mixed clients (Outlook desktop + Google Calendar) we usually do both: manually send an ICS and paste a calendar join link (Teams/Zoom) in the body.

I'll attach a quick ICS we can send that specifies TZID=Europe/Paris and a sample copy-paste body.

Marcus Lin
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
